The Git pipeline builds graph objects using model_directed_graph() and then applies projections and weighting on top of that. In contrast, the Depends and Understand pipelines stop at edge list outputs and do not construct graph objects inside Kaiaulu. Because of this, outputs from different pipelines are not directly interchangeable.

Perfect, this is one of the things I wish to fix in Kaiaulu. We want the "abstraction to be consistent" so they are interchangeable. This is a great word to stick to: We want to define good, well-defined interfaces so a bug in one output does not cascade everywhere else. It will also help a lot the exporter functions to DSM. One thing that is unique to Depends and Understand is that their tools output data already as networks (node, edgelist) or sometimes just edgelist. So I think some of this code tried to just massage the files on the fly to make do. We want to agree on a set of abstractions that outputs the same data structure of nodes and edgelist regardless.

I would recommend you also add three more diagrams: The mailing list transform for mbox, the github transform and the jira transform. These are the most used datasets and they provide enough variety for us to consider our new interfaces and abstractions will be consistent across all of them. See R/mail.R, R/jira.R, and R/github.R.

In essence we need to have a well-defined data type that should be expected as input. In turn, that data table with fixed column names and structure must be utilized by all functions that provide data to the transform. We never had the chance to go back and think through as we added new data sources, and that eventually led to this issue.

Your work here goes hand in hand with the person in another group working on the database schema. One of his milestones is to ensure a set of R functions that export tables in a consistent format. I am also considering whether we make a "interface" function. In Java, you can write both abstract classes and interfaces. These are wonderful to define the archetype of a class for anything that comes after. R is simpler as a language, and its class system is not the greatest (there are 3 systems!), but there is a more lightweight version of it that allows to ensure data types. There is one single lone example of that in the entirety of Kaiaulu, actually in graph.R:

## Experiment: Applying `model_directed_graph()` to Depends As part of Milestone 1, I ran an experiment applying `model_directed_graph()` to the output of the Depends pipeline. The objective was to determine whether Depends could be elevated to the same abstraction layer as GitLog and to identify what structural changes would be required. The Depends pipeline currently proceeds as follows: 1. `parse_dependencies()` invokes the Depends CLI and parses its JSON output into a structured object containing file-level nodes and a dependency-type edgelist. 2. `transform_dependencies_to_network()` collapses the dependency-type matrix into a weighted file-to-file network, producing `nodes(name, color)` and `edgelist(from, to, weight)`. At this point, the pipeline terminates and returns a weighted network representation. In the experiment, I applied `model_directed_graph()` directly to the weighted edgelist returned by `transform_dependencies_to_network()`. This produced a `directed_graph` object containing: - `nodes(name, type, color)` - `edgelist(from, to, weight)` Structurally, this matches the abstraction level produced by the GitLog pipeline. ### Comparison: GitLog vs Depends Comparing the revised Depends pipeline to GitLog reveals an important architectural difference. In the GitLog pipeline, graph abstraction is constructed inside the transform functions themselves. For example, `transform_gitlog_to_temporal_network()` generates an edgelist and immediately calls `model_directed_graph()`, after which projections and weighting logic are applied to the resulting graph object. The Git pipeline therefore transitions into the graph abstraction layer during transformation. In contrast, the current Depends pipeline produces a weighted network list but does not enter the graph abstraction layer unless `model_directed_graph()` is applied explicitly afterward. The experiment demonstrates that Depends can cleanly align with GitLog once this additional step is introduced. There is no structural difference in the inputs or outputs required by `model_directed_graph()` between the two pipelines. In both cases, the function expects an edgelist with `from`, `to`, and optionally `weight`. However, the semantic meaning differs. In GitLog, edges often represent developer-to-file relationships and may involve bipartite or temporal structures. In Depends, edges represent static file-to-file dependencies. The abstraction layer is therefore consistent, even though the domain semantics differ. ### Constructing a `model_undirected_graph()` Abstraction During this comparison, it also became clear that Kaiaulu currently assumes directed graphs as the default abstraction. While this is appropriate for many pipelines (such as commit or dependency flows), some data sources are conceptually symmetric. For example, co-change networks, co-authorship networks, or certain projections derived from GitHub, Jira, or mail replies may be better represented as undirected graphs. A `model_undirected_graph()` function could be constructed analogously to `model_directed_graph()`, but would normalize edge directionality before building the graph abstraction. Conceptually, this would involve: 1. Taking an edgelist with `from`, `to`, and optional `weight`. 2. Sorting or canonicalizing node pairs so that `(A, B)` and `(B, A)` are treated as the same edge. 3. Aggregating duplicate edges by summing weights where appropriate. 4. Constructing a graph object flagged as undirected. The resulting abstraction would maintain the same standardized schema for nodes and edges but remove directionality from the representation. This would allow pipelines that naturally produce symmetric relationships to converge to the same graph abstraction contract without artificially imposing direction. Introducing `model_undirected_graph()` would further support Milestone 2’s goal of defining consistent transform interfaces. Instead of each pipeline implicitly deciding whether it is directed or undirected, the abstraction choice would be explicit and standardized at the graph-construction layer. ### Implications for Standardization The experiment shows that the Depends pipeline can be aligned with GitLog at the graph abstraction level. Once `model_directed_graph()` is applied, both pipelines produce structurally consistent `directed_graph` objects with compatible node and edge schemas. The remaining differences are semantic rather than structural. Introducing both `model_directed_graph()` and a potential `model_undirected_graph()` abstraction would allow all pipelines to converge on a shared contract: ``` parse_* ↓ transform_*_to_network ↓ model_(directed|undirected)_graph ↓ projections / exports / metrics ``` Downstream projections, exports such as DSM, and analysis workflows could then operate uniformly on graph objects rather than pipeline-specific list structures. This experiment, therefore, not only validates the feasibility of standardizing Depends but also suggests a broader architectural improvement for Kaiaulu’s graph modeling layer moving forward.
